title: Paloma and the Playlist
premise: Quentin Iversen has spent four years at Hollowbrook Academy perfecting invisibility, but the senior college essay prompt — 'What song changed you, and why?' — forces her to confront the truth about the fire that killed her sister Paloma, a fire the school's beloved founding family helped cover up. When her playlist of Paloma's songs starts circulating and the school threatens her scholarship unless she recants, Quentin joins the girls' soccer team as the only route to a platform big enough to be heard. In the championship game, she trades the trophy for a microphone, telling Paloma's story to the whole gym — and walks out of Hollowbrook with no scholarship, but finally with her own name.
about_author: Sebastian Ravensworth is the pen name of a former high school debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers learn which truths are survivable. He writes from a converted boathouse in the Pacific Northwest, where he insists every draft must pass the 'would a seventeen-year-old roll their eyes?' test.

chapters.title: The Question on Page Three
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Senior year at Hollowbrook Academy: keep your head down, count the days. But the college essay prompt — 'What song changed you?' — stops her cold, because the honest answer is a song her dead sister used to sing. Emotional beat: the crack in the armor; invisibility starts costing something.

chapters.title: Static in the Walls
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She finds Paloma's old burned CD hidden in the school library's local history section, filed beside documents about the 2009 gymnasium fire — and a photo showing the Ashford family, Hollowbrook's founders, standing in front of the rubble, smiling. Beat: dread; the school is built over something it chose to forget.

chapters.title: Tryouts for the Invisible
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Coach Delgado, a former Ashford employee with her own guilt, all but begs Quentin to join the failing girls' soccer team — the only school event the whole town attends, and the only stage big enough for the truth. Quentin refuses, then sees her scholarship review notice. Beat: cornered; survival demands a price.

chapters.title: Paloma's Playlist
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with flashbacks to Paloma. Training montage interwoven with memories: how Paloma's mixtapes taught Quentin to speak, and how Paloma was working at the gym the night it burned, the night the Ashfords' son was driving. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Smiled at the Fire
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Theo Ashford — the founder's grandson, now a senior — joins the team as manager and is kind, funny, and genuinely drawn to Quentin. She realizes he may not know what his family did, and hates that she's starting to care. Beat: loyalty vs. truth becomes personal, not abstract.

chapters.title: What the Essay Was For
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She submits her real essay — naming the fire, the cover-up, the settlement that bought her family's silence — to her counselor, who quietly forwards it to the Ashford trustees. Within a day, Quentin is accused of plagiarism and suspended from the team pending review. Beat: the machine turns on her.

chapters.title: Theo Reads Page Three
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He finds the essay, cross-checks it against his grandfather's sealed letters, and realizes his family burned a girl's name to protect its own. He confronts his father and is disowned on the spot. Beat: the ally Quentin didn't dare hope for, at the cost of everything he had.

chapters.title: Eligibility
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The school offers a deal: recant, apologize, play the championship, get her scholarship and a glowing recommendation. Her mother, exhausted and scared, begs her to take it. Quentin signs — and plans to break the promise on the biggest stage in town. Beat: the terrible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating Quentin and Theo POV. Championship night, packed gym, scouts in the stands. Quentin plays the game of her life, then at the trophy ceremony takes the microphone, plays track one of Paloma's playlist over the speakers, and tells the gym exactly what the Ashfords did. Beat: climax — the championship that doesn't matter, won by losing it.

chapters.title: What Song Changed You
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, weeks later. The story goes national; the Ashford name is stripped from the gym; her scholarship is gone but a journalism program offers her a place based on the essay she actually wrote. She and Theo, both unmoored, drive past the rebuilt gym as Paloma's song plays. Beat: resolution — truth cost everything except the one thing that mattered.
